raw:
Seraphel’s smile comes properly this time.

“At times it does.  
Though poor rhymes are harmless.  
Poor manners have sharper teeth.”

She leads you down the stairs. The common room opens briefly at the landing: firelight on dark leather, portraits watching from above the mantel, a card table folded against one wall. Voices and the smell of peppered roast carry from the dining hall beyond.

The long table is set beneath working lamps and candles, though only one end is occupied. A tall demon woman with black-red horns sits with one boot hooked around her chair leg, studying the serving platters as if they have made tactical errors. Beside her, a carefully dressed beastkin man is saying something low enough that only she hears; his dark-furred hand rests flat beside his plate. Across from them, a white-haired woman sits very still, a glass of water beading untouched before her.

At the nearer end, an elf with silver hair looks up from the menu card she has apparently been reading for flaws. A small fae woman has claimed a chair sideways and is peeling the paper from a wrapped sweet. The angel in white and gold at the head of the table turns as you enter, his posture immediately formal.

The demon woman’s gold eyes settle on your signet, then your face.

“Bing Bong Garvey,” she says. “I’m Ashara vel Kothren. Sit down before Rashid starts introducing everyone by ancestry and voting record.”
